Shows the contacts stored on this phone next to the FRITZ!Box phone books. Needs access to your contacts; they never leave the phone.
Android does not allow Pickelhaube to read your contacts. You can allow it in the app settings.
Also offers the numbers dialled, received and missed with the phone’s own telephony app. Needs access to your call log; it never leaves the phone.
Only works if Pickelhaube was installed from outside Google Play (APK or F-Droid): Google Play allows reading the call log only for the phone’s default phone app.
Encrypted connection (port %1$d). The box’s self-signed certificate must be confirmed once.
The HTTPS port this FritzBox reported
Shows the contacts stored in this FritzBox’s phone books, including online phone books synced into it (e.g. CardDAV). They are read from the box when needed and not stored on the phone.
The numbers recently dialled, received and missed, from this FritzBox’s call list. Needs the permission “Voice messages, fax messages, FRITZ!App Fon and call list”.
%1$s does not have this permission on the box, so the call list cannot be read.

On the box, enable “Allow access for applications” (Home Network › Network › Network Settings) and “Dial help” (Telephony › Calls › Dial Help). The user needs telephony permission. If you log in with password only, use the auto-generated user name shown under System › FRITZ!Box Users.
Voice messages, fax messages, FRITZ!App Fon and call list
Not known yet. Read from the box on the next connection – unless its user lacks the rights for it.
None. When connecting via HTTPS you will be asked to confirm the router’s certificate.

The router presents a different certificate than the one you trusted before. This happens after a factory reset or a changed box name – but it could also mean someone is intercepting the connection. Only continue if you can explain it.

The router uses a self-signed certificate that cannot be verified automatically. Compare the SHA-256 fingerprint with the one your browser shows for https://fritz.box (or the certificate in the FRITZ!Box web UI) before trusting it.
This certificate is outside its validity period.
Your FRITZ!Box asks you to confirm this step before it carries it out.
• Press a button on the FRITZ!Box.
• Dial %1$s on a phone connected to the FRITZ!Box.
• Or dial %1$s on a phone connected to the FRITZ!Box.

The FRITZ!Box did not receive the confirmation in time. Tap Retry and confirm on the box (press its button, or dial the shown code on a connected phone).
The FritzBox at %1$s is not “%2$s”: its serial number differs from the stored one. If the box was replaced, delete this connection and add it again.
The FRITZ!Box currently blocks confirmations (too many attempts). Wait a few minutes and try again.
